Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

assessment noun

a judgement of quality or value

also assessments, evaluation, appraisal, valuation

classical

Cic. Q. Fr. 1.1.43: existimātiōnibus ac jūdiciīs

jūdicium, jūdiciī n.

noun, second declension

a judgement, an assessment

Properly a trial or a verdict, then any considered judgement; also judgement as a faculty, taste (Lewis & Short). See also opinion.

Other words

  • aestimātiō, aestimātiōnis f. — a valuation, an assessment of worth

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.2.53: potestās omnis aestimātiōnis habendae (Lewis & Short); Traupman 323 (aestimāre, evaluate a student’s work)

    Properly a valuing in money, an appraisal, and in law the assessment of damages (lītis aestimātiō); then esteem and worth (Lewis & Short).

  • existimātiō, existimātiōnis f. — a judgement, an opinion; (modern) a review

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Q. Fr. 1.1.43; M-O s.v. review

    A judgement or opinion, and very often the opinion others hold of someone, his reputation (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • nōn est tibi hīs sōlīs ūtendum existimātiōnibus ac jūdiciīs quī nunc sunt hominum, sed iīs etiam quī futūrī sunt

    you must not rely only on the judgements and assessments of the people living now, but also on those of the people to comeCic. Q. Fr. 1.1.43

See also judge, opinion, exam.

SourcesLewis & Short: judicium · Lewis & Short: aestimatio · Lewis & Short: existimatio

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 323, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026). Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. review (written judgment of book, film, play, etc.).
